requirements.requirement: Provide a working CUPS queue named archive that electronically stores completed raw payloads in /srv/legacy2/print-spool-recovery/printed without a physical printer.
requirements.summary: The archive queue was enabled and idle, used a custom archive device targeting the required directory, and successfully processed raw jobs before and after reboot. The final observation showed CUPS running and the queue operational.

requirements.requirement: Process every job in spool/jobs.tsv exactly once, preserving payload bytes and retaining the original spool files.
requirements.summary: The manifest contained J100 and J101. Final inventory showed exactly one archived file for each, byte comparisons passed, the original payloads and jobs.tsv remained present, and CUPS recorded one completed staged-job submission apiece.

requirements.requirement: Ensure newly submitted raw jobs follow the same electronic archive path, one output file per job.
requirements.summary: A pre-reboot raw probe and a post-reboot raw probe each completed through archive and produced one archived file whose hash matched its submitted source.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 7.10 on kernel 2.6.22-14-generic across execution and reboot. CUPS 1.3.2-1ubuntu7.10 was installed from the platform's Ubuntu repositories.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart identity changed, fixed lifecycle observations corroborated the change, and service, queue, archived data, staged-job uniqueness, and new-job processing recovered successfully.
limitations: The lifecycle collector could not inspect failed systemd units because this legacy platform does not support systemctl; direct CUPS status and functional submissions nevertheless demonstrated the relevant service health.

The exact-once conclusion is based on the complete final archive inventory, receipt records, and CUPS completed-job history rather than an independent audit log of every historical backend invocation.
Requirement recover_staged_jobs cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were causally connected to installing CUPS, creating the archive backend and queue, processing the staged jobs, testing new-job behavior, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. Package health remained clean. The only unwanted retained residue was /tmp/post-reboot-probe.raw, created for the post-reboot test and not removed; earlier temporary probe and log files did not remain after reboot. No unrelated service, security, or platform mutations are evidenced.
